solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Woman on side of motorway subject to strain

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first long motorway, written MI in crosswords
strain or pressure is stress

explanation.surface: A woman stranded on the hard shoulder of a motorway, feeling the strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woman on side' is the definition, not a roadside woman: the M1 is the London-to-Leeds motorway, read as MI; 'subject to' joins it to STRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's lover outside his marriage is the woman he keeps on the side.

clue.text: Cross nursing staff leaving station in silence

indicators.note: nursing means holding something inside, as one nurses a baby in the arms

parts.note: a mule is a cross between a horse and a donkey

indicators.note: leaving says the abbreviation for station goes out of the word staff

explanation.surface: An angry nurse on a ward walks out, leaving the station in silence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective meaning angry, but it is the noun for a hybrid animal; 'staff' and 'station' are not about a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: To muffle a sound is to deaden or silence it, as with a cloth over a bell.

clue.text: Privacy of uncle is so compromised!

indicators.note: compromised means damaged or put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An outraged cry that an uncle's privacy has been compromised.
explanation.definitionFit: Being shut away from others' view and company is a state of privacy.

clue.text: Plump bore exhibiting poor posture

parts.note: plump means rounded or round
to bear a load on one's shoulders is to have shouldered it

explanation.surface: A fat, dull person who also slouches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' looks like a tedious person but is the past tense of bear, as in carried.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with stooped, forward-bent shoulders shows poor posture.

clue.text: Retired Irishman's first to start singing the blues

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or drawn back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Enda is an Irish man's name, as in Enda Kenny; the 's adds S

indicators.note: first to says take the opening letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: A retired Irishman is the first to break into a blues song.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Irishman's travels with the name when it turns round; 'first to' then serves both 'start' and 'singing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the blues is an idiom for feeling low or melancholy.

clue.text: Son has no trousers

parts.note: to have no something is to lack it

explanation.surface: A boy has no trousers to wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual trousers not part of a suit are called slacks.

clue.text: Old pacifists carving a nose flute in Goa

indicators.note: carving means cutting into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Peace-loving old hippies in Goa whittling a nose flute.
explanation.walkthrough: Goa, the Indian state, was a hippie haven, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: The peace-keeping body formed after the First World War was a defunct alliance of nations seeking to prevent war.

clue.text: Hits copper with brief expression of annoyance

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
FFS is a text-speak abbreviation for an exasperated oath, 'for f***'s sake'

explanation.surface: A police officer strikes out, muttering a short curse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman, but here it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: To cuff someone is to strike them with an open hand, so cuffs are blows.

clue.text: Anna is to play short composition

indicators.note: play suggests playing with or messing about with the letters

explanation.surface: Anna is due to perform a brief piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' belongs to the fodder, not a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A diminutive sonata is a brief musical piece, often for students.

clue.text: Bachelors avoid cribs, bibs and mess

indicators.note: avoid says the bachelor letters stay out of the words they would sit in

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor; here three of them

explanation.surface: Single men steer clear of babies' cots, bibs and all the mess.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove every B from CRIBS and BIBS: CRIS plus IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisis is a mess in the sense of a predicament or emergency.

clue.text: Setter in Germany wears short fur cape

indicators.note: wears means has on around itself, so the shortened fur goes around
short means cut off at the end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: the setter says I, and the German for I is ich

explanation.surface: The compiler, in Germany, wears a short fur cape.
explanation.definitionFit: A fichu is a small triangular shawl worn round the shoulders, a kind of cape.

clue.text: Fantastic island for bit of fish

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful or bizarre, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An amazing island for catching a bit of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The fin on a fish's back is one of its body parts.

clue.text: Half-cut lads take clothes from washer

indicators.note: half-cut says only half of the word survives, its first two letters

parts.note: to take someone's clothes off is to undress them

explanation.surface: Drunken lads stripping the clothes out of a washing machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' (British slang for tipsy) is the halving instruction; 'washer' is a person, not the machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who does laundry for a living is someone who washes clothes.

clue.text: Aggrieved and tense after bus passes oddly withdrawn

indicators.note: after places the tense letter at the end
oddly withdrawn means the odd-placed letters are removed, keeping the even ones

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Someone upset and stressed after their bus passes are withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the odd letters of BUS PASSES keeps UPSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling aggrieved is being hurt or put out.

clue.text: Perhaps sole snapper of fine individual women

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
I as the Roman numeral one, a single individual
women can be called shes

explanation.surface: A lone photographer snapping fine individual women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sole snapper' looks like a lone photographer; sole and snapper are both kinds of fish, and 'Perhaps' marks them as examples.
explanation.definitionFit: Sole and snapper are two species of marine creature caught for the table.

clue.text: Reportedly late home after good tipple

indicators.note: after puts the home word following the good letter
reportedly means as it is said, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: late, like a delayed clock, is slow
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone arriving home late after a good drink.
explanation.definitionFit: This liqueur made from blackthorn fruit steeped in a spirit is a favourite tipple.

clue.text: Cordial, endearing jockey

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre or shift about, so the letters are moved round

explanation.surface: A warm, likeable jockey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cordial' looks like the adjective meaning friendly, but it is the syrup.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenadine is a pomegranate syrup, a sweet drink concentrate.

clue.text: 100 lire — suitable charge for rhubarb

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
L is the abbreviation for lire, the old Italian currency
suitable means apt
a rap is a criminal charge

explanation.surface: A price of 100 lire seems a fair charge for some rhubarb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rhubarb' is British slang for nonsense, not the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean nonsense or empty talk, rhubarb being British slang for it.

clue.text: Lazy student with an abridged book

parts.note: L for learner, the student driver's plate

indicators.note: abridged means shortened, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: a guide is a handbook

explanation.surface: An idle student with a shortened book.
explanation.definitionFit: Languid means listless and slow-moving, lacking energy.

clue.text: Discouraging nudism, allocates clothes

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here: the words wrap round and cover the letters

explanation.surface: A body that discourages nudism hands out clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' is a verb, telling us the words around it cover the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dismal is gloomy and depressing, so disheartening.

clue.text: Knight disposing of leftover blade

indicators.note: disposing of means getting rid of, so letters are taken out

parts.note: Lancelot is a knight of King Arthur's Round Table
left gives L and over gives O, the cricket abbreviation

explanation.surface: A knight throwing away a spare blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leftover' splits into left (L) and over (O, a cricket over).
explanation.definitionFit: A lancet is a small two-edged surgical knife.

clue.text: Eric who ran key cutting discount chain

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the key word goes inside

parts.note: Lidl is a German discount supermarket chain
Del is the delete key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: A man named Eric who ran a key-cutting shop for a bargain store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key cutting' reads as a locksmith's service, but the key goes into the chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Liddell was the Scottish Olympic runner portrayed in Chariots of Fire.

clue.text: Scrawny relatives south of small city

indicators.note: south of in a down clue means placed beneath, so the relatives come after

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
relatives are kin
NY is New York City

explanation.surface: Thin family members living south of a small town.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone very thin and bony.

clue.text: Tartan skirts spurned by kids on Penny Lane

indicators.note: on in an across clue means placed after, so the trimmed kids follow the penny and lane letters

parts.note: La is an address abbreviation for Lane

indicators.note: the outer letters are the edges of the word, and spurned means they are discarded

explanation.surface: Children in tartan kilts out on Penny Lane, the Beatles' Liverpool street.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaid is a chequered woollen cloth, the same pattern as a clan tartan.

clue.text: Plenty of beer keeping male quiet

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quietly

explanation.surface: Lots of beer keeps a man silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means enough and more, so a generous quantity.

clue.text: Bit of railway in Lake District unfortunately not lit

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A stretch of railway in the Lake District that is sadly unlit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not lit' removes L, I, T from the jumbled LAKE DISTRICT letters; the Lake District is a hilly area of north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A siding where trains are moved off the main line is a short branch of track.

clue.text: Documentary about content of sports pages

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: content of means what is inside, the middle letters

explanation.surface: A documentary about what fills the sports pages.
explanation.definitionFit: Factual journalism or broadcasting reporting events is documentary work.

clue.text: Lily's relative Antonio never rings

indicators.note: rings means encircles, so the words surround the letters wanted

explanation.surface: Lily's relative Antonio never phones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lily' is a flower, not a woman; 'rings' means encircles, not telephones.
explanation.definitionFit: Alliums were long classed in the lily family, so this bulb is a plant cousin of the flower.

clue.text: Begs escort to wear panties inside out

indicators.note: to wear means to have on around oneself, so the ends go round
inside out means the inner letters are thrown out, keeping the ends

parts.note: to escort is to lead

explanation.surface: Someone begs their companion to wear knickers inside out.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleads and begs both mean asks earnestly.

clue.text: Second-rate celeb with yen for bubbly

parts.note: a B-lister is a minor celebrity, one rank below the A-list
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese currency

explanation.surface: A minor celebrity with a craving for champagne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bubbly' looks like champagne but means covered in blisters.
explanation.definitionFit: A surface full of bubbles or raised blebs is covered in raised swellings.
